name: AK Cep
description: A Cepheid in the Milky Way that pulsates every 7.23 days; its mean radius is 59.5 solar radii.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, AK Cep: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 59.5 +/- 9.7 (Monte-Carlo)

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 359, Name='AK Cep', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5375 +/- 168 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic)

distance.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, AK Cep: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 4035.8 +/- 628 (Monte-Carlo)

color.reason: Interstellar dust reddens every spectrum of this star, E(B-V) = 0.635 +/- 0.049 (Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10), and its light changes through each pulsation

text.card: A Cepheid in the Milky Way that swells and shrinks every 7.2 days.
text.introduction: Its mean radius, 59.5 solar radii, comes from comparing how fast its surface moves with how its size changes, 4,036 parsecs away.
text.locator: table10, AK Cep: Per, Rad, Dist

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius.
No dynamical mass is measured for this Cepheid; its mass is left unmeasured.

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)
